smartphone.title: Smartphone
smartphone.subtitle: Your main camera
smartphone.text:
Modern smartphones like the iPhone 15 Pro, Samsung S24 Ultra, or Google Pixel 8 offer features that were reserved for pro cameras just years ago:

  • RAW capture for maximum editing flexibility
  • Multiple focal lengths (Ultra-Wide, Standard, Tele)
  • Pro modes for manual exposure, ISO, and shutter speed
  • Night mode for impressive low-light shots
  • Computational Photography for HDR and Portrait mode

The best part: You always have it with you. The best shot is the one you can actually take.
smartphone.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Use Pro/RAW mode for maximum quality and editing flexibility
  • Clean the lens before every shoot — fingerprints are the #1 reason for soft images
  • Use the fixed optical cameras instead of digital zooms
  • Hold the phone with both hands and brace your elbows

stativ.title: Tripod
stativ.subtitle: Stability for sharp images
stativ.text:
A tripod is essential for long exposures, HDR images, and any shot where the camera needs to stay absolutely still.

Options for every budget:

  • Joby GorillaPod — bendable legs, clamps anywhere
  • Neewer Tabletop Tripod — €20, solid quality
  • Manfrotto Compact — professional, but pricier
  • DIY — stack of books, bag as counterweight

On the go: Any flat surface works. Be creative!
stativ.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Use the self-timer (3s) to avoid vibrations from tapping
  • For landscapes: Place tripod on solid ground, not wooden planks
  • A small sandbag as counterweight makes lightweight tripods more stable
  • In wind: Hang your camera bag as a counterweight under the tripod

licht.title: Light
licht.subtitle: The most important element
licht.text:
Good light does more for your photo than a more expensive camera. Bad light destroys high-resolution images — good light saves every shot.

Free light sources:

  • Window light — soft, natural, perfect for portraits
  • Overcast sky — natural diffusion outdoors
  • White wall / cardboard — as a reflector for indirect light

Budget upgrade: A single LED panel with softbox (€30) dramatically improves your shots.
licht.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • The "golden hour" (1h after sunrise / before sunset) is magical
  • Use a white cardboard as reflector to fill harsh shadows
  • Avoid mixed lighting (daylight + tungsten) — it creates color casts
  • In strong backlight: Use HDR mode or expose for the background

power.title: Power Bank
power.subtitle: Never run out of battery again
power.text:
RAW photography and long photo days drain the battery fast. A power bank is not a luxury — it's insurance against the worst moment: "Battery low" in the middle of your best shot.

What you need:

  • At least 20,000 mAh for a photo day
  • USB-C PD for fast charging (30W+)
  • Several short cables (0.3m) instead of one long one

Pro tip: Charge during breaks — many smartphones support continuity charging.
power.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Enable "airplane mode" while shooting — saves 30% battery
  • Dim the display to 30% between shots
  • Use a 0.3m USB-C cable — less cable clutter
  • Label your power bank — on locations, things get mixed up

reinigung.title: Cleaning
reinigung.subtitle: Clarity for every detail
reinigung.text:
A dirty lens is the silent killer of good photos. Dust, fingerprints, and grease obscure details, reduce contrast, and create light spots.

The right equipment:

  • Microfiber cloth — soft, lint-free, reusable
  • Blower — removes dust without touching
  • Lens cleaner — for stubborn dirt
  • No paper tissues! — scratches guaranteed

Care tip: Keep the microfiber cloth in a clean bag.
reinigung.tips:
Pro Tips:
  • Clean the lens before every shoot — not just when it's visibly dirty
  • Blow dust away first before wiping with the cloth
  • Wipe in circular motions from center to edge
  • For smartphones: Also clean the back lens — often overlooked
